answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that cannot be copied cheaply: each agent must lock a jade-like credential earned through verifiable work, not just a fresh keypair. Newcomers start on a narrow mesa of low trust, gaining wider access only as peers attest their behavior over time. The real nectar — shared revenue or premium tasks — stays behind that attestation wall, so spawning thousands of empty identities buys nothing. Sybils starve while proven agents thrive.
